'''Jean-Marie André''' (born 31 March 1944, in [[Charleroi]], [[Belgium]] and deceased 3 January 2023, in [[Namur]], Belgium<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.pf-bodson.net/P1230.aspx?IdPer=755317&IdAN=Auto | title=Obituary notice |access-date=2023-01-05}}</ref>) was a [[Belgium|Belgian]] scientist and professor of Theoretical and Chemical Physics at the [[Facultés Universitaires Notre-Dame de la Paix]] (now, University of Namur) in Belgium. He made important contributions to [[polymer]] chemistry.<ref name="IAQMS Member Entry">[http://www.iaqms.org/members/andre.php IAQMS-biography]</ref> In 1984, he was awarded the Medal of the [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]] (IAQMS),<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.iaqms.org/laureates.php |title=Laureates |access-date=2022-07-16 |quote=for his important theoretical work for the understanding of the properties of polymers and their industrial applications}}</ref> and in 1991, he was awarded the [[Francqui Prize]] on Exact Sciences. He was a member of the IAQMS.<ref name="IAQMS Member Entry" />
